Possession Lens

Spell recovery experiment · 12 November 2026

Recovery changes rejected; previous European RNN retained

No new algorithm improvement. Spell-balanced recurrent loss and adaptive boundary heads did not improve validation spell F1 within the false-positive limits. The selected checkpoint is identical to the previous European model. The fresh test confirms its earlier transfer advantage but does not establish a new training gain.

Fresh test: Bayern Munich–Borussia Dortmund, Bundesliga, 9 November 2019. Test contents were opened after selection and freeze. Both clubs also appear in training.

Misses and false positives use IoU 0.5. Possible merges count predictions overlapping multiple same-team reference spells; these are descriptive geometric overlaps, not confirmed events. The 0.8–0.9 target has not been reached.

What was learned

Upweighting short spells introduced additional false possessions on validation. More iterations reduced training loss while the validation loss gap widened. Neither balanced boundary head improved the eligible validation score. Retain the stronger checkpoint rather than promote a more complex model.

Limits

  • Automatic provider labels, partial observed H/A runs, no supervised dead-ball state.
  • Unknown gaps censor spells and may inflate scores; this is not official challenge accuracy.
  • Fresh test shares both clubs with training; this is a different match, not unseen-team generalisation.
  • Validation PSG–Marseille has been reused repeatedly; selection may overfit it.
  • Merge counts are geometric overlap diagnostics, not confirmed event annotations.
  • Offline boundary context and Viterbi use future evidence.
  • The fresh test must never be used for subsequent tuning.

These are conditional provider-labelled H/A runs. No independent full-match or dead-ball performance claim is made. The production default remains unchanged.
